agents.name: Claude Code

surface_source.quote:
1. install Claude Code
2. open your terminal of choice in your Obsidian vault folder
3. run > claude command

agents.quote: I'm starting a set of Claude Skills for Obsidian... so far they're centered around helping Claude Code edit .md, .base, and .canvas files

review_style.value: Recorded test output must be read; fixture must fail before the fix
review_style.quote: This writes the output and **fails intentionally**. Read the new files or `git diff`, then rerun without `UPDATE_EXPECTED`. A recording that nobody reviews is not a useful check.

also.quote: Always run `--dry-run` first so the user can review the changeset before publishing.

harness.value: Agent verifies changes in the running Obsidian app through Obsidian CLI
harness.quote: The check requires the Obsidian CLI, the plugin enabled in the target vault, and the current source built and deployed there. It uses `E2E_VAULT` when set; otherwise it derives the vault from `OBSIDIAN_PATH`. It writes `_e2e-check` and trashes that folder after the run.

rules_files.value: AGENTS.md in Defuddle (CLAUDE.md until 2026-09-20), 188-line CLAUDE.md in Obsidian Importer
rules_files.quote: Always use `curl` to test the Worker or defuddle.md; never open those URLs in a browser.

signature.caption: before every extraction fix
signature.why: Our pick: his rules make the agent prove a bug with a failing fixture before fixing it, and forbid editing expectations to fit.
signature.quote: For extraction fixes, add a minimal HTML fixture in `tests/fixtures/` with correct expected output in `tests/expected/`. Verify the same fixture fails before the fix and passes afterward; do not change expectations to match buggy behavior.

archetype.why: Writes long, precise rules files (security, fail-first fixtures, reviewed recordings) for the repos he codes in.

signature_quote.value: As hyped as Claude Code + Obsidian is, I have no desire to upload my personal unencrypted vault data to Anthropic or anyone else.
signature_quote.more: I hope that the ideas of private inference and confidential computing that @moxie described take off. It's how all LLMs should work.
